claim: The engineered pay run reviewer (a defined role, a fixed procedure, worked examples that are not the test case, and the meaning of every code) gave the same judgement in twenty reviews on the attested NEAR AI Cloud model: a planted line with no tax withheld was caught in 10 of 10 reviews with the identical finding, a corrected run was passed in 10 of 10, and none of the 20 had a false claim
limitations: One model at temperature 0, two synthetic runs of four lines, from this machine
It shows repeatability on this input, not general accuracy on payroll
The model has no authority on tax law; it is told to reason only from the employer's rules
The test passed on the first brief written, so there is no record of failed drafts

Re-run on 2026-11-13 on the final brief (sha256 765247d1… in the hardware run's evidence; the repository's current brief), after a first run on an earlier brief (docs/lab-runs/20261113T034712Z-5244 and 20261113T034504Z-c6cd, kept as history)

claim: Scored against right answers worked out by code from the numbers, the engineered pay run reviewer on the attested NEAR AI Cloud model caught 47 of 47 planted mistakes on 30 held-out generated runs and 12 of 12 on 16 hand-designed hard cases (boundaries 0.1 point from a limit, a stated tax rate of 0, a cap of 0, fractional rates, eight-line runs), with no false claims in 69 checkable findings and every clean run left clean; the same test found and drove the fix of two real faults in the first brief (a missed boundary and invented findings under tiered rules)
limitations: Small samples: 47 and 12 planted mistakes, 9 and 4 clean runs
Synthetic runs, the four codes the brief names, one model at temperature 0, one review per run
The right answers read the same rounded numbers the model is given, so this measures applying the employer's stated rules and not real payroll judgement
The brief was improved against the development set; only the held-out and hard sets are honest estimates, and each was run once with the brief frozen
Two earlier development rounds failed or were spoiled and are kept locally, not promoted

claim: A pay run that names an approver is not signed by the room until that approver, a different account from the employer who prepared it, signs an approval bound to the round, the run id and the run's order hash with a key the chain says belongs to the approver's account; the approver receives a sealed summary of the run; approval and signing each happen once; without an approver the pay run behaves as before
limitations: Offline on a local room with a stubbed account-key check; the hardware run is a separate experiment
The contract does not check the approval; the room does, inside the attested hardware
Two accounts can belong to one person
The approver is named in the run request, which only the coordinator sends; it is not fixed in the group's public rules, so the coordinator could name a second account it controls (GAP-055)

claim: On a real Phala TDX VM running the hosted Roost, an employee pay run with no invoices settled on the production contract with exact amounts after an attested AI review caught a planted line with no tax withheld and a separate approver (not the employer who prepared the run) signed off: the room refused to sign before the approval and refused an approval signed with another key, the approver's sealed summary matched the run, the private tax and benefits lines added up to the single public transfers, every payslip verified against the order hash read from the chain, and the auditor pack opened only the line the employer signed for
limitations: One operator ran the room and every account
The approver is named in the run request by the coordinator, not fixed in the public rules (GAP-055); the contract does not see the approval, the room checks it
Amounts and addresses are public on NEAR
The mistake is planted
A settlement pays at most 8 recipients (GAP-053)

claim: On a real Phala TDX VM running the hosted Roost, a block trade crossed sealed, signed firm orders at a public reference price: a buyer whose limit was under the reference price was left out, the smaller sell side filled in full and the buy side pro rata, the published outcome carried no limit price, and the production contract paid the sellers and charged the buyers exactly the reference price times their filled units
limitations: One operator ran every account
Only the middle of a block trade is modelled: no indications of interest or firm-up step, no minimum fill, no time priority, a supplied reference price, and only the cash leg settles
Charges and payouts are public, so filled units can be worked out from the cash and the reference price
A first attempt stopped at its own preflight check because the previous VM was still listed while being deleted; it spent nothing and is kept locally

claim: The room models four more real-world states, each proven offline with mutation checks: a quote past its validUntil is left out and named while the best valid invited quote wins and an uninvited maker is ignored; a cross order filled below its minUnits is cancelled and the cross recomputed until no fill is below its minimum, publishing only how many were cancelled; a vote with an explicit null share moves no money and signs a decision that a browser verifies and that can never be settled or reopened; and the AI reviewer's saved model receipt verifies in a browser only when its signed text, signer and ed25519 signature all hold
limitations: Offline, on a local room with a simulated attestation provider, a stubbed account-key check and a fixed clock
Expiry uses the VM's own clock, which its host could skew
A decision-only vote is signed by the room and not recorded on chain; the contract cannot record a result with no payment
The model receipt check proves the signature and the key it names, not that the key belongs to an attested model; that attestation is still only reported
Not modelled: a challenge period before a payout, the firm-up step for block trades, last look (left out on purpose: it lets a dealer back out after acceptance)
